newsitem.title: UK: N. Irish police probe blast in Catholic Belfast.
newsitem.headline: N. Irish police probe blast in Catholic Belfast.

text.p: Northern Irish police said on Thursday they were investigating an explosion in a Catholic area of east Belfast.
Security sources said an ambulance had been sent to the scene and there might have been injuries. A British security forces patrol was in the area at the time.
The sources said the incident might have been an attack by Irish Republican Army guerrillas fighting to end British rule.

"All we know is a patrol was in the area and an explosion occurred. An ambulance has been sent to the scene. It looks as though there are injuries but we don't know how many or how serious," one security source said.
The blast happened in the Short Strand district, a Catholic enclave in the largely pro-British Protestant east of the city.
Earlier on Thursday a British soldier was hurt when suspected IRA guerrillas threw a grenade at an armoured vehicle in north Belfast.
